name: Dimmer DIN Rail Module
description: A dimmer module that mounts on a DIN rail in an electrical panel to dim and switch lighting circuits remotely. It supports adjustable brightness levels and ramp rates.

steps.text: Turn off the breaker or fuse and make sure the power is off.
Disconnect the wires from the light fixture and strip them to 5/16 inch (8 mm) of bare wire.
Making sure the wires are not touching, turn on the breaker or fuse.
Use a voltage meter to identify the fixture's line, load and neutral wires.
Turn off the breaker or fuse again.
Write down the Insteon ID on the side of the module and the load it controls.
Snap the module onto the DIN rail. Next to another module, leave 3/4 inch (2 cm) between them for heat dissipation.
Connect the line, load, neutral and sense wires per the diagram for your installation.
Make sure the wires are firmly connected with no exposed wire.
Turn on the breaker or fuse.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the load turns on and the LED turns green

steps.text: Tap the module's paddle top and bottom to test it.
steps.expect: The load turns on and off; LED green when on, red when off

steps.text: For a single or dual momentary wall switch, set the switch operation mode: press and hold the SET button until it beeps three times.
steps.expect: Three beeps; LED blinks green, red, then green

steps.text: Slowly tap the SET button four times for single momentary or five times for dual momentary.
Press and hold the SET button until it double-beeps.

notes: Neutral is required. The module ships set for a latching wall switch; tap six times instead to switch back to latching.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.

notes: As a controller: after the module beeps, set the responder to the state to recall and press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps. The module double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.

As a responder: press and hold the controller button until it beeps, press and hold the module's paddle top or bottom to set the load to the level to recall (or off), then press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps.
A link is one way. For a group such as a virtual 3-way circuit, link both directions.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the device's reports.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, adjust it to the desired scene brightness or state.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.
Tap On, Off or the SET button once to exit multi-linking.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Press and hold the SET button until it beeps a second time.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.
steps.expect: The module double-beeps and its LED stops blinking

notes: To remove the module as a responder: press and hold the controller button until it beeps, press and hold it again until it beeps a second time, then press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps.

steps.text: Remove the module's scene memberships from all controllers.
Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
Press and hold the SET button until it beeps a second time.
Press and hold the SET button until it beeps a third time.
Slowly tap the SET button 3 times.
Press and hold the SET button and don't let go.
Release the SET button after the beeping stops.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the module double-beeps, turns on and its LED turns green

steps.text: Remove the module as a controller of each of its responders.
Remove all of the module's responder links from its controllers.
Uninstall the module.

notes: Otherwise controllers retry commands repeatedly, creating network delays.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove every link between the Hub and the device with no SET button press. First the device's group 1 link: Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) is sent to the device while the modem joins as responder. Then the modem's group 0 link: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09).

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as the Dimmer DIN Rail Module 2452 Owner's Manual gives it, clears them.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: HouseLinc also lists its identity under 2252-222.
